name: Two desks, one daily P&L
brief:
Two desks report daily P&L in pounds as pandas Series `a` and `b`, each on a sorted date index named `date`. They do not report on the same days. The firm's P&L on a day is the sum of what was reported; a desk that did not report that day counts as 0.

Write `combined_pnl(a, b)`. It returns a Series over every day on which at least one desk reported, in date order. The tests compare values with `tolist()`, floats within a relative `1e-9`, and the dates as text. The helper `on(dates, values)` builds a Series to try.

Example. Desk `a` reports 1,200, -300 and 450 on 2, 3 and 5 June. Desk `b` reports 200, -150 and -50 on 3, 4 and 5 June. The answer is 1,200, -100, -150 and 400 on 2 to 5 June.
constraints: Either Series may be empty. No reported value is missing.
pandas is available. All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Turn each Series into a frame with `reset_index()` (new here: it turns a Series into a frame with a `date` column), then `pd.merge(..., on="date", how="outer")`. Fill the gaps with 0 before adding, and sort by date.
starter:
import pandas as pd

def combined_pnl(a, b):
    # your code here
    return a

examples.note: On 4 June only desk `b` reported, so the total is its -150.
Every day either desk reported, in date order.

how: Submit runs 11 hidden tests. Lists are compared item by item. Each float counts when it is within a relative `1e-9` of the expected value; text and whole numbers must be equal.
where: Draws on numpy-pandas lesson l13-joining-on-dates: an outer join on the date.
solution:
import pandas as pd

def combined_pnl(a, b):
    left = a.rename("a").reset_index()
    right = b.rename("b").reset_index()
    m = pd.merge(left, right, on="date", how="outer").sort_values("date")
    total = m["a"].fillna(0) + m["b"].fillna(0)
    return pd.Series(total.to_numpy(), index=pd.DatetimeIndex(m["date"], name="date"), name="pnl")
notes: An outer join keeps every date found in either Series and leaves NaN where a desk did not report.
The NaN must become 0 before the sum, because NaN plus a number is NaN.
One merge on the date, about $O(n \log n)$ with the sort.
